candidate_delta: None. The qualification ran in a separate worktree checked out at the tag commit and recorded that commit and an empty working-tree patch (the digest above is that of an empty patch).

sandbox_image.distribution: The image published to GitHub Container Registry for 0.9.11, pulled with scripts/pull-sandbox.sh on 2026-11-25 (ghcr.io/henrycooper86/oxfuzz-fuzz-sandbox@sha256:44b0b5f951634e368e5ed8acb25da84b3ab8a12913ac6fddddf6c23d3620677d) and tagged with the local name. 0.9.12 and 0.9.13 use the same image as 0.9.11.

review: Provider review passed before execution for all three engines, using a local Ollama model (qwen3:8b), as for 0.9.11 and 0.9.12. Explicit human approval was supplied for this exact source pair on 2026-11-27; the pair is unchanged since 0.9.10.
limitations: One short cycle per engine does not establish long-duration stability or a statistical latency percentile.
No crashes occurred; crash reproduction and symbolization are not claimed by this cycle.
Executed on macOS arm64 with a Linux arm64 Docker sandbox; not a Linux desktop installation test. Windows is not supported.
The pre-execution review used a small local model rather than the provider configured for the desktop app.

This cycle covers C sources on libFuzzer, AFL++ and honggfuzz. The binary-only engine has its own 0.9.13 record; the Go, Python, Java and JavaScript engines were not rerun, and their last live results are the 0.9.8 related record, made on a different commit.
The qualification drives the service operations from a test, not from the desktop app.

The Docker socket was named with DOCKER_HOST (OrbStack's socket), because this host has no /var/run/docker.sock and the runs redirect HOME. A first attempt without it failed every isolation test before any container started; that attempt is kept with the evidence and is not counted.
